method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.claims: TACO can include hypertension/venous congestion; delayed haemolytic reactions typically occur after24 hours, median1–2 weeks. Supports137/138 clinical premise, not current distractor quality.
Primary Canadian paediatric source opened for sickle-cell complication context; source-specific facts require matching section, not blanket authorization of every nursing action.

items.assessment: The saturation-versus-oxygen-content concept is useful, but discarding the haemoglobin result is an implausible competitor.
issues: The saturation-versus-oxygen-content concept is useful, but discarding the haemoglobin result is an implausible competitor.
proposedChanges: Replace the discard-result option with a plausible inference, such as using an oxygen-response trial to decide whether anaemia explains the symptoms.

items.assessment: Pacing is appropriate, but every distractor visibly undermines safe independence.
issues: Pacing is appropriate, but every distractor visibly undermines safe independence.
proposedChanges: Compare plausible activity plans: rest before a standing shower, partial assistance with a usual shower, shorter hygiene at the basin, or seated shower with breaks. Add context that makes one plan best; avoid making all reasonable alternatives correct.

items.assessment: The acute chest-symptom priority is sound; iron-rich foods and oral iron after lunch are too remote from current instability.
issues: The acute chest-symptom priority is sound; iron-rich foods and oral iron after lunch are too remote from current instability.
proposedChanges: Ask which new finding changes urgency or compare relevant immediate assessments rather than nutrition tasks.

items.assessment: Thrombocytopenia and increasing headache justify urgent review, but after-sleep and before-deciding clauses advertise delay.
issues: Thrombocytopenia and increasing headache justify urgent review, but after-sleep and before-deciding clauses advertise delay.
proposedChanges: Use plain competing actions such as analgesia, a focused previous-headache history, and local injury assessment; explain their insufficient priority in the rationale.

items.assessment: Specific positioning and direct pressure are foundational first aid; common head-back, flat-position and clot-disruption errors make this a useful technique item.
Prompt authorized analgesia is correct, but all three alternatives explicitly postpone it, leaving one humane and reasonable answer.
issues: Prompt authorized analgesia is correct, but all three alternatives explicitly postpone it, leaving one humane and reasonable answer.
proposedChanges: Compare credible pain-management plans, such as usual PRN sequence, individualized episode plan, previous effective dose verification, and nonpharmacological support alongside rather than instead of medication; contextualize why the individualized plan leads.

items.assessment: New hypoxaemia suggests acute chest complications, but a longer walk and a cup of fluid are conspicuously poor alternatives.
issues: New hypoxaemia suggests acute chest complications, but a longer walk and a cup of fluid are conspicuously poor alternatives.
proposedChanges: Use parallel clinical interpretations or relevant competing assessments. Do not make exercise during distress a distractor.

items.assessment: Hydration tolerance is useful, but unprescribed rate increase and ignoring respiratory signs are weak competitors; challenge difficulty is inflated.
issues: Hydration tolerance is useful, but unprescribed rate increase and ignoring respiratory signs are weak competitors; challenge difficulty is inflated.
proposedChanges: Compare possible overload, acute chest, simple dehydration, or expected analgesic-related findings, or provide a more discriminating ordered-fluid evaluation; use application unless substantial integration is added.

items.assessment: The caregiver-baseline and sequestration cues are clinically useful, but snack/next-week-ultrasound/routine-documentation alternatives make the emergency obvious.
issues: The caregiver-baseline and sequestration cues are clinically useful, but snack/next-week-ultrasound/routine-documentation alternatives make the emergency obvious.
proposedChanges: Compare possible causes of the changed presentation (sequestration, vaso-occlusive pain, medication sedation, aplastic crisis) or ask for the most informative immediate finding. Keep no definitive independent PN diagnosis.

items.assessment: Protection and the authorized haemostatic plan address suspected joint bleeding; early range of motion and massage are recognizable but inappropriate rehabilitation errors.
The preserved-component task is distinct and correct, but reconnecting a serious-reaction bag is a poor competitor and application difficulty overstates recall.
issues: The preserved-component task is distinct and correct, but reconnecting a serious-reaction bag is a poor competitor and application difficulty overstates recall.
proposedChanges: Use credible handling alternatives, such as return labelled bag only, retain bag and tubing, discard after documenting identifiers, or send a new recipient sample only; classify foundation.

items.assessment: TACO pattern is supported, but mild isolated allergy and local IV reaction do not meaningfully compete with pulmonary congestion.
issues: TACO pattern is supported, but mild isolated allergy and local IV reaction do not meaningfully compete with pulmonary congestion.
proposedChanges: Use TACO, TRALI, acute haemolysis, and anaphylaxis as parallel concerns; explain the relative support from hypertension and venous congestion without claiming certainty.

items.assessment: Delayed haemolysis timing is valid, but next-month review and waiting for fever advertise wrong answers.
issues: Delayed haemolysis timing is valid, but next-month review and waiting for fever advertise wrong answers.
proposedChanges: Use parallel explanations of the jaundice/urine/fatigue pattern, or plain competing advice without arbitrary delay clauses.

items.assessment: Afebrile neutropenic shock is important, but warm-drink temperature repeat, sleep and next scheduled blood count are cartoon delays.
issues: Afebrile neutropenic shock is important, but warm-drink temperature repeat, sleep and next scheduled blood count are cartoon delays.
proposedChanges: Ask which data cluster requires emergency response or which handover interpretation is best, with plausible shock differentials; consider application rather than challenge.

items.assessment: Severe mucositis affecting intake and medicines merits coordinated review, but rough food and dose reduction are implausible alternatives.
issues: Severe mucositis affecting intake and medicines merits coordinated review, but rough food and dose reduction are implausible alternatives.
proposedChanges: Use plausible competing plans such as pre-dose topical pain care, requesting liquid formulations, arranging IV hydration review, or comprehensive route/pain/hydration review with balanced option length and enough context for one best response.

items.assessment: Severity and dehydration support urgent oncology contact; juice, next visit and extra doses beyond the plan are conspicuously weak.
issues: Severity and dehydration support urgent oncology contact; juice, next visit and extra doses beyond the plan are conspicuously weak.
proposedChanges: Compare the supplied lower-grade home-care steps with the oncology escalation step using a brief protocol exhibit or clinically credible alternative actions.

items.assessment: TLS pattern is useful, but without-investigation, correcting-itself and next-cycle qualifiers telegraph rejection.
issues: TLS pattern is useful, but without-investigation, correcting-itself and next-cycle qualifiers telegraph rejection.
proposedChanges: Use parallel mechanisms such as tumour-cell breakdown, dehydration-related renal retention, treatment-associated SIADH, or poor intake; explain the distinctive combined urate/phosphate/potassium/calcium pattern.

items.assessment: Stem states supine worsening and the key repeats the obvious opposite; face into pillow is unsafe filler.
issues: Stem states supine worsening and the key repeats the obvious opposite; face into pillow is unsafe filler.
proposedChanges: Replace with a different SVCS task, such as identifying the pattern requiring urgent review among clinical findings, or compare meaningful supportive plans without face-obstruction distractors.

items.assessment: Cord-compression cues are clear, but routine physiotherapy, walking and before-contacting clauses make the answer guessable.
issues: Cord-compression cues are clear, but routine physiotherapy, walking and before-contacting clauses make the answer guessable.
proposedChanges: Use a discriminating neurological assessment/interpretation task or credible immediate actions with plain wording.

items.assessment: SATA distinguishes emerging fluid-related harm and persistent metabolic effects from combined clinical/laboratory improvement.
Protecting a suspected pathological fracture is correct, but repeated movement, standing and massage are an all-unsafe distractor set.
issues: Protecting a suspected pathological fracture is correct, but repeated movement, standing and massage are an all-unsafe distractor set.
proposedChanges: Compare supporting the limb, administering ordered analgesia, assessing distal neurovascular findings, and contacting the team; define whether the task asks first physical action, most informative assessment, or handover concern.

items.assessment: Acute inflammation with fever warrants review, but vigorous massage/tighter sleeve/future appointment advertise poor care.
issues: Acute inflammation with fever warrants review, but vigorous massage/tighter sleeve/future appointment advertise poor care.
proposedChanges: Use normal compression care, measured circumference, elevation, and infection assessment as plain plausible competing responses; preserve context that acute systemic signs change the priority.

items.assessment: The correct comfort-care principle is valid, but withholding assessment, forcing meals and limiting discussion to girth are caricatures.
issues: The correct comfort-care principle is valid, but withholding assessment, forcing meals and limiting discussion to girth are caricatures.
proposedChanges: Give realistic competing symptom plans and client preferences, such as adjusting meal size, positioning, scheduled symptom medication review or discussion of therapeutic drainage; ask which addresses the stated priority.

items.assessment: Moist desquamation needs reassessment; fragranced lotion, direct tape and scrubbing are cartoon skin-care choices.
issues: Moist desquamation needs reassessment; fragranced lotion, direct tape and scrubbing are cartoon skin-care choices.
proposedChanges: Compare plausible skin-care plans, such as continuing a prior dry-skin emollient plan, protective nonadherent dressing assessment, saline cleansing, or topical steroid request, with sufficient context and authority for a single best answer.

items.assessment: This repeats bowel-obstruction recognition in110/111/115; cancer context alone does not create a distinct task, and fluid/fibre alternatives are weak.
issues: This repeats bowel-obstruction recognition in110/111/115; cancer context alone does not create a distinct task, and fluid/fibre alternatives are weak.
proposedChanges: Use malignant-obstruction care under explicit comfort goals, evaluating symptom control or route of delivery rather than repeating recognize-and-call; keep 200 items through replacement.
